label: b52: ffr2d2 (feed-forward control, dense 512 in the LSTM place), seed 8 of 12, 1.3M steps = 41.6M moves, 130k updates
notes: Batch b52, Group E row E2 (plans/algoExploration/e-memory.md section 2, 2b): R2D2 (Kapturowski et al. 2019) as the paper has it, in one process on 32 lanes. LSTM 512 after fc 320 with the previous action one-hot and the raw previous reward as cell inputs, dueling 512-wide streams, scalar Q; windows of 120 stored rows = 40 burn-in prefix + 80 loss steps (the paper's m = 80, l = 40), a new loss block every 40 steps so adjacent windows overlap by 40 (the paper's section 2.3), cut per episode from its first step (0 burn-in at the start, from the zero state; a 20-step episode is one window); burn-in on online and target from the stored (h, c) under no_grad; squared TD on the 5-step double-Q target under h(x) (eps 1e-3, rewards unclipped), summed over the block, IS-weighted (beta 0.6, max-normalised), averaged over 64 windows; PER alpha 0.9, priority 0.9 max + 0.1 mean of |TD|, new windows at max priority (a stated departure); Adam 1e-4 eps 1e-3, hard target copy every 2,500 updates, grad clip 40; Ape-X epsilon ladder 0.4^(1 + 7 i/31) over the 32 lanes, held. hist8, b2 reward, step penalty 0.01, shaping OFF (the paper-cell rule). THE BUDGET IS THE UPDATE COUNT (decided 2026-09-30; the paper's own run is ~190k updates: 5/s over 10B frames at 256 x 260 steps/s): SNEK_REPLAY_RATIO 1/320 gradient steps a move x 1.3M counted steps x 32 moves = 41.6M moves and 130,000 learner updates (52 target copies). SHORTFALL, stated: 130k against the 200k working floor / the paper's ~190k -- the longest wave that fits ~24 h on the desktop. Benchmark 2026-09-30, laptop solo, 1 thread, under load: LSTM update 517 ms at the paper's 125-slot window (240 ms at 85 slots), collector 1.5 ms a 32-lane step, dense update 100 ms, sample 0.5 ms, RSS 1.4 GB at 20k windows -- the learner is the limit, 130k updates ~ 19 h solo / ~27 h in a 4-arm desktop wave at 0.7x if the under-load figure holds, ~24 h if a clean box gives back the load; the dense cell ~5x faster. 64 x 80 = 5,120 loss rows an update = 16 loss rows a move against the paper's 0.8: a deliberate adaptation, the same in every cell of this batch, so within-batch readings are clean and only the comparison to the paper's regime carries it. Replay 30,000 windows (~1.6 GB an arm with the unroll's activations; the box has ~12.8 GB free). Three cells of 4 seeds: r2d2paper (a-d); ffr2d2 (e-h, SNEK_R2D2_RECURRENT=dense: the paper's own section 4 feed-forward ablation, Linear 512 + ReLU in the LSTM's place, no state, the SAME windows, loss positions, priorities, targets, moves, updates and batch -- memory alone is paper minus ffr2d2); r2d2c51 (i-l, SNEK_R2D2_HEAD=c51 SNEK_R2D2_RESCALE=0: C1's categorical head on the support [-10, 110] under the memory, the rescaling off because the support is the return itself -- two recipes against the paper cell, not the distribution alone). Read: paper against ffr2d2 (memory), paper against b46's Rainbow paper cell and b35's DQN paper cell for shape, c51 against paper. Registered prediction (the agent, 2026-09-30): the paper cell reaches 90%+ perfect inside 41.6M moves and holds (the ladder's low-epsilon lanes and the 0.997 horizon suit this game), ffr2d2 trails it by a clear margin on the hold (drawdowns, sef) but not on the peak, and the c51 cell is level with the paper cell within noise; none reaches PPO's 99.8 hof30k row. Stage A every 1,000 counted steps = 32k moves (PPO's cadence), 1,300 evals an arm.
